clue.text: American with knight welcomed by adorable king

indicators.note: the first pieces are welcomed, taken in, by the word for adorable, so they sit inside it

parts.note: adorable means cute
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: An American and a knight are greeted warmly by a charming monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: A and N go inside CUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Canute was an eleventh-century ruler of England, Denmark and Norway, famous for the tale of commanding the tide.

clue.text: Stylish clothing provided in catalogue

indicators.note: clothing means dressing, wrapping round, so the stylish word encloses the other

parts.note: classy means stylish
if means provided, as a condition

explanation.surface: Fashionable outfits are included in a shopping catalogue.
explanation.definitionFit: To classify is to sort into categories, as one does when cataloguing items.

clue.text: Giant also upset shows sentimental feeling

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sporting giant, also upset, grows sentimental.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia is a wistful longing for the past, a sentimental yearning.

clue.text: Poet initially stuck in loo turned up

indicators.note: in puts the single letter inside the reversed toilet word
in a down answer turned up means read from bottom to top, so reversed

parts.note: loo is British slang for toilet

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A poet trapped in a toilet that has been turned over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses TOILET into TELIOT, and S, from 'initially' on 'stuck', goes in after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: T. S. Eliot was the American-born British poet who wrote The Waste Land.

clue.text: Dalmatians most unlikely to be this pure

definitions.text: Dalmatians most unlikely to be this
definitions.meaning: first meaning: literally without spots, which a spotted Dalmatian never is

explanation.walkthrough: One reading is the literal one, having no spots, which rules out a Dalmatian; the other is the figurative sense of unblemished.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without a stain or flaw is described as spotless, the everyday figurative sense of having no marks.

clue.text: Men cope: friends somehow showing calmness in crisis

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Men cope with friends, somehow staying calm in a crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: Presence of mind is the ability to think clearly and act quickly in an emergency.

clue.text: Saint feeding unpleasant person a fried tortilla

indicators.note: feeding means going into, as food goes into a mouth

parts.note: a toad is a contemptible, unpleasant person

explanation.surface: A saint feeds a nasty person a Mexican snack.
explanation.definitionFit: A tostada is a Mexican tortilla crisped by frying and topped with beans, meat or salad.

clue.text: Tummy bug? Tablet reduced abdominal cramps!

parts.note: E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: colic is severe abdominal pain

explanation.surface: A tummy bug: a pill brings down the stomach cramps.
explanation.walkthrough: COLIC reduced loses its last letter to give COLI.
explanation.definitionFit: E. coli is a gut bacterium, some strains of which cause food poisoning; the question mark flags 'bug' as a germ.

clue.text: Guard observed protecting credit

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding to shield, so the observed word goes around

parts.note: seen means observed
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: A guard is seen protecting someone's credit rating.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen shields or protects something, so to screen is to guard.

clue.text: Such funds as Labour won't ever secure?

definitions.text: Such funds as Labour won't ever secure?

parts.words: Such funds as Labour won't ever secure?
parts.note: money got without work: labour never earns it, read with Labour as the UK political party

explanation.walkthrough: Labour with a capital looks like Britain's Labour Party; the cryptic reading is labour as work, which never earns this money.
explanation.definitionFit: Investment returns such as dividends and interest come in without work, so economists call them by this name.

clue.text: One succeeded stocking beer in supermarket lane

indicators.note: stocking means holding inside, as a shop stocks goods, so the beer word contains the others

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
I is the Roman numeral for one
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: Someone who got ahead by stocking beer, picturing a supermarket shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: I and S go inside ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is the walkway between shelves in a shop, the lane shoppers push their trolleys along.

clue.text: Danish physicist fixed NHS boiler

indicators.note: something fixed is put back in order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Danish scientist repairs a boiler for Britain's National Health Service.
explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is the UK's National Health Service.
explanation.definitionFit: Niels Bohr was the Danish scientist who modelled the atom's structure and won the Nobel Prize in 1922.

clue.text: Resilience enlivens pirouettes? No energy needed!

indicators.note: a pirouette is a spin on the spot, so the letters turn round and read backwards
no energy means the letter for energy is dropped

parts.note: to animate something is to enliven it
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A dancer's pirouettes need resilience, though apparently no energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No energy needed' drops E from ANIMATES to give ANIMATS, and 'pirouettes' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is staying power, the endurance to keep going, which is a sense of resilience.

clue.text: Devious woman tempted to hold back travel permit

indicators.note: the first word is to hold the second inside it

parts.note: Eve, the first woman, was tempted by the serpent in Eden

indicators.note: back means the permit word is read in reverse

parts.note: a visa is a permit to travel to a country

explanation.surface: A shifty woman is tempted to withhold someone's travel papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns VISA into ASIV, which EVE holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone evasive dodges questions and avoids being straight, much like a devious, shifty person.

clue.text: Decent prospect of beating the odds?

definitions.text: Decent prospect of beating the odds?

parts.words: Decent prospect of beating the odds?
parts.note: a reasonable chance of success, and also a chance of 'beating' read as fighting

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is an idiom for a real possibility of success; 'beating' hints at the fighting in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a realistic possibility of succeeding against difficulty if one makes a big effort.

clue.text: Nuncio led astray finds seventh heaven

indicators.note: astray means off course, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A papal envoy led off the right path finds bliss.
explanation.walkthrough: A nuncio is a papal ambassador.
explanation.definitionFit: Both idioms mean a state of supreme happiness or bliss.

clue.text: European media thus covers something stimulating

indicators.note: covers means encloses, so the thus word wraps round the media word

parts.note: so means thus
the press means the news media

explanation.surface: European news outlets thus report on a stimulating story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' looks like the press reporting a story, but it is the container signal: the word for thus wraps round the media.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso is strong black coffee, a drink valued for its caffeine kick.

clue.text: As man had kitty, fresh meat so brought round in dish

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are brought round the other pieces, enclosing them
fresh means new, so these letters take a new arrangement

parts.note: he'd is a contraction of he had, he being a man
a kitty is a pot of pooled money

explanation.surface: A man with a pet cat cooks fresh meat into a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled 'meat so' splits round the middle pieces, one letter in front and five behind; 'man had' is the contraction he'd, with its apostrophe dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Mashed potatoes are a side dish of boiled potatoes pounded smooth, commonly with butter and milk.

clue.text: Label put into socks for prisoner

indicators.note: the label word is put into the socks word

parts.note: hose is an old word for stockings or socks
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A name label is sewn into a prisoner's socks.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostage is a person held captive as security for demands, effectively a prisoner.

clue.text: Native American artist parking in two areas by house

indicators.note: in puts the artist and parking letters inside the two area letters

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for area, twice
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A Native American painter parks across two zones beside a house.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arapaho are a Native American people of the Great Plains, now in Wyoming and Oklahoma.

clue.text: Reportedly one able to provide alien craft?

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken, so the word is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a sourcer is one who sources, able to provide something

explanation.surface: A dubious claim about who might supply a spaceship.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent SOURCER and SAUCER sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A flying saucer is the disc-shaped spaceship of UFO lore, so an alien craft.

clue.text: Mechanic in a star that's collapsing

indicators.note: something collapsing falls apart, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A mechanic is inside a collapsing star, a science-fiction disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled manual worker; 'mechanic' in its older sense means a craftsman who works with hands.

clue.text: Catches on thin branches

definitions.meaning: first meaning: British informal for understands, catches on

explanation.walkthrough: To twig is British slang for to realise.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the plural noun for slender shoots and a verb meaning grasps or realises.

clue.text: Snake seen in Rome and Eritrea

indicators.note: the answer can be seen lying inside these words

explanation.surface: A snake is spotted in both Italy's capital and Eritrea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snake' looks like the reptile but is the verb, to wind about.
explanation.definitionFit: To meander is to follow a winding course, just as a road or river is said to snake.

clue.text: Feature to pull in an ethnic community

parts.note: the chin is a feature of the face

indicators.note: in places the pulling word inside the word an

parts.note: to tow is to pull

explanation.surface: Some attraction draws people into an ethnic neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feature' means a part of the face here, not an attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinatown is a district of a city where Chinese people have settled, a distinct ethnic quarter.

clue.text: One young woman not quite right

parts.note: a means one
miss is a title for a young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A girl who is a bit off, or out of sorts.
explanation.definitionFit: When something is amiss it is wrong or out of order, slightly off.

clue.text: Sounding healthy, vegetable chopped for tea?

indicators.note: sounding means the next word is heard rather than spelt as given

parts.note: rosy, as in rosy cheeks, means healthy-looking

indicators.note: chopped means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a leek is a vegetable

explanation.surface: A healthy-sounding vegetable is chopped up for the evening meal.
explanation.walkthrough: ROSY is said aloud as ROSIE; LEEK is chopped to LEE. Rosie Lee is Cockney rhyming slang for tea, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang, Rosie Lee rhymes with and stands for the drink tea.

clue.text: Well soggy duck in Johannesburg settlement

parts.note: well in the sense of very, so
soggy means wet
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, the letter O

explanation.surface: A soaked duck wanders through a South African township.
explanation.definitionFit: Soweto is the large township south-west of Johannesburg, central in the anti-apartheid struggle.
